classification.difficultyReason: Select the clockwise angle from north; part c additionally requires transferring the given angle between parallel north references before finding the bearing.

content.prompt: Give the true bearing of $A$ from $O$.

spec.description: North–south reference through O; A southeast of O; 30° between south and OA. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 30-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
A true bearing is measured clockwise from north.
$$\begin{align*}b&=180^\circ-30^\circ\\b&=150^\circ\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: North ray from O; A northwest of O; 42° between north and OA. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: OA is 42 degrees west of north.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 42-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
Measure clockwise from north through the larger angle.
$$\begin{align*}b&=360^\circ-42^\circ\\b&=318^\circ\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A southeast of O, with parallel vertical north references at both endpoints and matching upward arrow marks. The angle at A between AO and north is 53°. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The north references are parallel; the angle east of south at O equals 53 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: The 53-degree angle remains at A; no bearing answer appears.

answer.worked:
The north references are parallel, so $OA$ makes an angle of $53^\circ$ east of south at $O$.
$$\begin{align*}b&=180^\circ-53^\circ\\b&=127^\circ\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: North–south reference through O; A southwest of O; 72° between south and OA. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: OA is 72 degrees west of south.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 72-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
Measure clockwise from north through south to $OA$.
$$\begin{align*}b&=180^\circ+72^\circ\\b&=252^\circ\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$
